Maya: FYI I'm getting a small but consistent token drift when long contexts hit a kernel change mid-run. Observed with mixed-precision where activation quant is FP8 (e4m3) and some layers fallback to BF16.
Owen: repro? which model/config? :thinking:
Maya: llama-2-7b, --quant fp8, max_seq=4096, batch=4. Single-batch looks clean, multi-batch shows drift after layer ~20.
Chandra: any logs or a tiny repro script? could be a KV address math bug during stride switch.
Maya: repro command and key log snippet below. This is from the micro-harness with --profile.
```
./run_infer --model llama2-7b --quant=fp8 --max-seq 4096 --batch 4 --profile --seed 42
```
Log slice:
```
[2026-03-10 14:12:31] KVCache: write_pos=2048 header_slot=31
[2026-03-10 14:12:31] MatmulDispatch: chosen_kernel=fp8_gemm_fast
[2026-03-10 14:12:31] MatmulDispatch: fallback_kernel=bf16_gemm_safe (layer=20)
[2026-03-10 14:12:31] QuantPack: pack_bytes=6144 pad=128 scale=7.8125e-03
[2026-03-10 14:12:31] KVCache: expected_index=2049 actual_index=1025  <-- mismatch
```
Owen: that actual_index looks like a half-page / element-size misinterpretation. Does it only show up when the fallback happens mid-sequence?
Maya: yes. Force all-FP8 or all-BF16 and it disappears. Mixed path + batch>1 reproduces.
Eli: likely cause: stride/offset arithmetic uses bytes_per_element in one place and element counts in another when kernels switch; packing metadata isn't normalized on fallback.
Chandra: can you bisect whether it's tied to quant_scale change or element width change?
Maya: bisected: triggers when quant_scale drops by >2x at the fallback boundary AND the kernel switches element-size from 1->2 bytes. Microbench attached shows deterministic behaviour.
PerfBot: microbench (same harness): FP8-only: 680 tok/s; BF16-only: 510 tok/s; Mixed-fallback: 460 tok/s. Flamegraph: https://perf.internal/redwood/fg/1755558888
Owen: mixed slower than BF16-only — that suggests extra repacking + unaligned writes on the hot path.
Maya: dumped nearby KV header bytes around the boundary (hex):
```
... 00 00 08 00  20 00 04 00  ff ff 01 00  ...
```
We expect element-count words but see leftover packed-byte offsets from previous FP8 layout.
Chandra: probable root: Matmul dispatcher recomputes buffer stride using runtime.bytes_per_element but doesn't inform KVCache that its header/offsets are in a different unit. Missing handshake/fence.
Eli: quick mitigation ideas:
- dev-assert comparing kv.header.seqlen vs runtime.seqlen on read
- on kernel switch, call KVCache::normalize_offsets(old_width, new_width) to convert header fields
- add unit test with long alternating fallback pattern validating first N tokens vs float32 baseline
Maya: I prototyped a fix that runs normalize_offsets on kernel switch; harness runs 1000 iterations with no mismatch.
Owen: normalize_offsets is O(#kv_slots) though which will kill perf on big contexts.
Chandra: optimize with lazy-fixup: track a per-chunk "offset_unit" flag and only apply delta on reads or when we compact. Update base header O(1). That avoids touching every slot on the hot write path.
PerfBot: lazy-fixup benchmark: mixed fallback throughput improves to 625 tok/s (vs 680 FP8-only). Correctness restored.
Maya: pushed a CI regression test: eng-runtime/mixprec-kv-boundary that runs two seeds x batch4 x seqlen4096 and diffs first 128 tokens to float32 ref (fails without fixup).
InfraBot: CI job created: eng-runtime/mixprec-kv-boundary/1755558888
Eli: micro-optimization: when quant scales are exact multiples, just reinterpret the buffer view instead of memcopy repack. Adds a small win for common cases.
Chandra: plan: land lazy-fixup + view-reinterpret, add dev-assert and CI test. Follow-up perf pass to try to recover the remaining ~8% gap.
Maya: opening PR with patches, tests, and flamegraphs. tagging @Chandra for review.
Maya: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4281 (WIP)
Owen: add final perf numbers & regression test id to PR description. Also create a backend telemetry alert to surface KV index mismatches in customer fleets.
PerfBot: created regression ticket PERF-2319.
Chandra: once this lands let's backfill a small fleet telemetry event and a postmortem doc template in case we see similar mismatches on other models.
Maya: thanks, will follow up with the telemetry plan and an investigation checklist.
